text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000226 bills 99215 about five times the risk-adjusted expectation, but the sampled records largely support the billed level, so the pattern is not clearly upcoding or a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The excess is not explained by panel mix: the 99215 share runs well above the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions (e.g., C0114066, R10.9 only; C0114103 and C0114282, the same depression patient), and the provider bills no 99211/99212 at all. Against that, 15 of the 16 documented 99215 claims were supported, with only C0114209 falling below (moderate MDM, no time), which on its face looks like a genuinely complex practice. That reassurance is limited because records cover only about 15% of claims, no audit trail was received, about 11% of notes repeat time entries, and 4 notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test on the claim. Those are weak signals that the notes could be templated to match billing, not proof. A reviewer should first pull additional charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims and request the EHR audit trail to test whether the supporting MDM and time documentation is cloned or reflects the actual visit."}
